items.title: Leaked clips reveal Google's Gemini Omni video model ahead of I/O 2026

featured_image.name: Gemini Omni Outperforms Veo 3.1 in Leaked Demo Videos

items.description: A new AI video generation model called Gemini Omni has surfaced inside Google's Gemini app in two waves of leaks, setting the stage for what could be a major announcement at Google I/O 2026 on May 19.[1][2]

items.title: Russia launches over 200 drones as U.S.-brokered ceasefire expires

featured_image.name: Russia, Ukraine resume strikes as ceasefire expires, report ...

items.description: Hours after a three-day ceasefire brokered by U.S. President Donald Trump expired at midnight on Monday, Russia launched 216 drones across Ukraine overnight into Tuesday, striking residential buildings, energy infrastructure, a kindergarten, and transport facilities in what Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called a deliberate choice to "end the partial silence that had lasted for several days."[1][2]

items.title: Pakistan calls CBS report on Iranian jets at airbase 'misleading'

featured_image.name: Pakistan allowed Iran to park military aircraft on its airfields despite  mediator role in conflict with U.S. - CBS News

items.description:
Pakistan's Foreign Office on Tuesday dismissed a CBS News report alleging that Iran parked military aircraft at Nur Khan Airbase near Rawalpindi to shield them from potential American airstrikes, calling the claims "misleading and sensationalised" and warning they could undermine ongoing peace efforts in the region.[1]

The rebuke came after CBS News reported on Sunday, citing anonymous U.S. officials, that Tehran had sent multiple aircraft — including an Iranian Air Force RC-130 reconnaissance plane, a surveillance variant of the Lockheed C-130 Hercules — to the strategically located airbase days after President Donald Trump announced a ceasefire with Iran in early April.[2][3]

items.title: Lebanon urges US pressure on Israel to halt raids as ceasefire frays

featured_image.name: Lebanon urges US to put pressure on Israel to stop attacks and demolitions  | Reuters

items.description: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called on the United States on Monday to pressure Israel into halting military strikes, ceasefire violations, and the demolition of homes in southern Lebanon, raising the issue directly with US Ambassador to Lebanon Michel Issa. The appeal came as Israeli airstrikes continued to pound southern Lebanon despite a ceasefire declared in mid-April, with Lebanon's health ministry reporting dozens killed in recent days.[1][2]

items.title: Lebanon asks US to pressure Israel to halt raids ahead of talks

featured_image.name: Lebanon urges US to put pressure on Israel to stop attacks and demolitions  | Reuters

items.description:
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called on the United States on Monday to pressure Israel into halting military operations and home demolitions in southern Lebanon, raising the issue directly with US Ambassador Michel Issa ahead of a pivotal round of peace talks later this week.[1][2]

The appeal came as Lebanon's health ministry reported that 74 people had been killed by Israeli strikes in just three days, pushing the total death toll since March 2 to 2,869, including 584 medics, women, and minors. More than 1.2 million people — over a fifth of Lebanon's population — have been displaced from their homes since the conflict escalated.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Trump weighs military action as Iran ceasefire talks collapse

featured_image.name: Trump weighs military action against Iran with ceasefire "on life support"

items.description:
President Donald Trump convened his national security team on Monday to discuss resuming military operations against Iran after dismissing Tehran's latest ceasefire proposal as "garbage" and declaring the fragile truce is on "massive life support," according to Axios, which cited three U.S. officials.[1]

The meeting comes after Iran communicated its response to the most recent U.S. peace proposal through Pakistani intermediaries on Sunday, only for Trump to reject it within hours on social media as "TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE."[2][3]

items.title: Pentagon reveals nuclear submarine's location in rare message to Iran

featured_image.name: Message To Iran: Navy Sends Guided-Missile Submarine On Rare Trip Into The  Persian Gulf (Updated)

items.description: The Pentagon took the unusual step on Monday of publicly acknowledging that a nuclear-armed ballistic missile submarine had arrived in Gibraltar on Sunday, May 10, in what analysts view as a calculated pressure signal directed at Iran as ceasefire negotiations collapse.

items.title: Iran deploys 'trigger-ready' submarines in Hormuz strait standoff

featured_image.name: Iran's IRGC Navy launches maritime drill in Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Iran's Navy confirmed on Sunday that its domestically built Ghadir-class midget submarines are operating in a "trigger-ready" state inside the Strait of Hormuz, escalating an already volatile maritime confrontation with the United States that has paralyzed global shipping through the world's most critical oil chokepoint.

items.title: CENTCOM says 62 ships redirected under Iran blockade

featured_image.name: U.S. Central Command to enforce maritime blockade on Iranian ports

items.description: The United States Central Command announced on Monday that more than 20 American warships are actively enforcing the naval blockade against Iran, with forces having redirected 62 commercial ships and disabled four others since operations began on April 13.[1][2][3]

items.title: Turkey set to receive first-ever US emergency oil shipment

featured_image.name: Turkey set to receive its first shipment from US emergency oil stash |  Reuters

items.description:
A cargo of crude oil from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve is heading to Turkey, marking the first-ever shipment of American emergency reserve oil to the Mediterranean nation, according to ship tracking data reported by Reuters.[1]

The delivery comes as the United States ramps up exports from its emergency stockpile to allies struggling with severe supply disruptions caused by the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a chokepoint through which roughly 20 percent of the world's oil trade normally passes.[2][3]

items.title: Brazilian flotilla activist returns home alleging torture by Israel

featured_image.name: Brazilian flotilla activist returns home, alleges torture during Israel  detention | Reuters

items.description:
Brazilian activist Thiago Ávila returned to São Paulo on Monday after being deported from Israel, where he alleged he was tortured and witnessed abuses of Palestinian prisoners during 10 days in custody following his arrest aboard a Gaza-bound humanitarian flotilla.[1][2]

"My return was simply a correction of a serious violation. I was kidnapped by Israel, I wasn't imprisoned," Ávila told reporters after his arrival at São Paulo-Guarulhos International Airport.[2]

items.title: Trump to press Xi on Iran at Beijing summit this week

featured_image.name: Iran war adds tension to Trump-Xi summit in China

items.description: President Donald Trump will use his trip to China this week to pressure Chinese President Xi Jinping over Beijing's support for Iran, including its purchase of Iranian oil, sales of dual-use goods, and potential weapons exports to Tehran, a senior White House official said Sunday.[1][2]

items.title: Japan pushes for New Zealand to choose Mogami-class frigates over UK rival

featured_image.name: Japan, UK Compete to Supply Warships for New Zealand Navy Upgrade -  Bloomberg

items.description:
New Zealand has shortlisted Japan's upgraded Mogami-class frigate and Britain's Type 31 as the two contenders to replace its aging warships, setting the stage for a closely watched competition between Tokyo and London that carries broad implications for Indo-Pacific defense ties.

Defence Minister Chris Penk confirmed on May 7 that New Zealand has entered formal discussions with Australia and the United Kingdom on the frigate replacement, with a recommendation expected to reach the government by the end of 2027. The two Anzac-class frigates under consideration for replacement — HMNZS Te Kaha and HMNZS Te Mana — were commissioned in 1997 and 1999, respectively, and most of the navy's fleet is projected to reach the end of its design life by the mid-2030s.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran says 35 million people face water shortages as crises mount

featured_image.name: Iran faces unprecedented drought as water crisis hits Tehran

items.description: Iranian authorities warned on Monday that approximately 35 million people face water shortages heading into summer, as a convergence of drought, a U.S. naval blockade, mass layoffs, and a prolonged internet blackout pushes the country toward what analysts describe as a deepening domestic crisis.

items.title: Knesset passes law creating military tribunal for Oct. 7 suspects

featured_image.name: 'A modern Eichmann trial': Lawmakers, justice minister tout ...

items.description:
Israel's Knesset on Monday voted overwhelmingly to establish a special military tribunal to prosecute Palestinians detained during and after the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks, creating a legal framework that could lead to death sentences for those convicted of genocide and other charges.

The legislation, which passed its second and third readings with broad bipartisan support, establishes a dedicated military court in Jerusalem to try an estimated 350 to 400 suspects captured inside Israel between October 7 and October 10, 2023. The bill was co-sponsored by Religious Zionism MK Simcha Rothman and opposition lawmaker Yulia Malinovsky of Yisrael Beytenu.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Pakistan let Iran park warplanes on its airfields

featured_image.name: Iran submits response to latest US ceasefire proposal via ...

items.description:
Pakistan quietly allowed Iranian military aircraft to park at its airfields during the US-Iran conflict, even as Islamabad positioned itself as the central diplomatic broker between Washington and Tehran, CBS News reported on Monday, citing US officials with knowledge of the matter.[1]

The revelation complicates the image Pakistan has cultivated as a neutral intermediary in a war now in its tenth week, raising questions about how Islamabad balanced competing loyalties during one of the most volatile periods in the broader Middle East conflict.

items.title: EU set to sanction violent Israeli settlers after Hungary lifts veto

featured_image.name: Kaja Kallas, The EU's new Foreign Affairs Chief

items.description:
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Monday she expects a political agreement on sanctions targeting violent Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, a measure that had been blocked for months by Hungary under former prime minister Viktor Orban.[1][2]

"I expect political agreement on the sanctions on violent settlers, hopefully we will get there," Kallas said ahead of a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels, though she cautioned it was "still not entirely clear the required majority would be found".[3][2]

items.title: MSF suspends operations in Haiti's Cité Soleil as gang clashes force hospital evacuations

featured_image.name: Hospitals evacuated, MSF services halted as rival gangs clash in Haiti's  capital | Reuters

items.description: Hospitals in the Cité Soleil neighborhood of Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince, evacuated their patients on Monday as Doctors Without Borders suspended all operations in the area amid escalating clashes between rival armed groups, according to Reuters. The violence, which intensified over the weekend, has left the densely populated district — home to hundreds of thousands — without a single functioning hospital.[1][2]

items.title: IDF sentences soldiers for desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon

featured_image.name: Photo shows Israeli soldier desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon

items.description:
The Israeli military on Monday sentenced two soldiers to military prison after one was photographed placing a cigarette in the mouth of a statue of the Virgin Mary in the southern Lebanese village of Debel, the second act of desecration against Christian symbols in the same village in recent weeks.

The soldier seen in the photograph received 21 days in military jail, while the soldier who took the photo was sentenced to 14 days, the IDF said. The sentencing was carried out by Brig. Gen. Sagiv Dahan, commander of the 162nd Division, who oversaw the relevant area of southern Lebanon at the time, according to the Times of Israel.[1][2]

items.title: EU's Kallas says Putin is 'weaker than ever' on Ukraine

featured_image.name: BELGIUM-EU-UKRAINE-CANADA-DIPLOMACY

items.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters on Monday that Russian President Vladimir Putin is "in a weaker position than he has ever been before," following a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels where the bloc adopted new sanctions over Russia's forced deportation of Ukrainian children and advanced plans for a more active European role in potential peace talks.
